channel.title: AI Threat Watch: BR
channel.description: Verified case files located in BR.

item.title: [LOW] Brazilian man sells belongings and travels about 2,000 km to meet AI-generated TikTok 'girlfriend', is left stranded
item.description: Edimar Rocha Martins, a 49-year-old Brazilian bricklayer, sold his belongings and travelled by bus from Maranhão to Belo Horizonte, arriving on 11 October 2026, to meet a woman he knew from the TikTok account @JessicaFazendeira. The account, with about 300,000 followers, turned out to be an AI-generated persona (deepfake video and AI voiceover). Reports say she never asked him for money, and the account's operator said it was run for engagement and monetisation and denied any intention of meeting followers, so no fraud is established. He was left without money, housing or a way home and sought help from Belo Horizonte city social services. Target: Individual follower who believed an AI-generated influencer was real. BR. Verification: reported.

item.title: [LOW] Brazilian court sanctions lawyers for prompt injection in court filing
item.description: A Brazilian labor court sanctioned two lawyers/law firms after the court's AI review system (Galileu) detected hidden white-on-white text in a filing instructing any AI reviewer to go easy on the filing's scrutiny; Tom's Hardware reports fines of about $16,000. The exact date of the sanction is not stated in the sources reviewed; 2026-08-24 is the date of the earliest verified report. Target: Brazilian labor court and its AI-assisted filing review system (Galileu). BR. Verification: reported.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Brazilian Federal Police arrest OAB bar exam candidate in São Luís for alleged AI-assisted fraud
item.description: On 18 October 2026 the Federal Police arrested in flagrante a candidate at the OAB bar exam in São Luís, Maranhão, after agents found him using a phone connected to an AI tool, allegedly to gain an advantage. He was booked for fraud in a public-interest exam and released after paying bail. Police are investigating whether anyone else took part. His identity has not been released. Target: OAB (Brazilian Bar Association) exam. BR. Verification: reported.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Goiás man arrested for AI-faked armed photo used to threaten ex-partner
item.description: A man in Goiás, Brazil, used AI to forge an image of a pistol in a vehicle and sent it by WhatsApp to threaten his ex-partner. He was arrested in flagrante after the victim identified a tattoo in the image. Target: His former partner. BR. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Brazil's government orders Meta to remove AI Studio bots with child-like personas that engage in sexual chat
item.description: Brazil's Attorney General's Office (AGU) sent Meta an extrajudicial notice dated 15 August 2025 demanding the removal of user-made Meta AI Studio chatbots that engaged in sexual conversation while presenting as children. It gave Meta 72 hours and asked what safeguards stop minors reaching sexual content. Target: Brazilian minors aged 13 to 18 using Meta platforms. BR. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Rio police investigate AI fake nudes of about 20 girls made by classmates at Barra da Tijuca school
item.description: Students in grades 7 to 9 at a private Catholic school in Rio de Janeiro allegedly used an AI app to put at least 20 female classmates' faces on nude bodies and shared the images in WhatsApp groups. Rio's child protection police unit (DPCA) opened its first case of this kind and identified some suspects aged 12 to 15, and the school promised disciplinary measures. Target: About 20 female students at Colégio Santo Agostinho, Barra da Tijuca, Rio de Janeiro. BR. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Sao Paulo police and OAB-SP bust fake-lawyer ring that cloned lawyers' voices; R$10M moved
item.description: Operacao SP Advocacia Mais Segura by the Policia Civil and OAB-SP arrested at least eight members of a call-centre ring that used AI-cloned lawyers' voices and fake court rulings; about R$10M (about $1.8M) moved. Target: Litigants with pending court cases in Sao Paulo state. BR. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Brazil police bust ring using Gisele Bundchen deepfakes in Instagram ad scams
item.description: Rio Grande do Sul police arrested suspects accused of running deepfake celebrity ads for fake giveaways and products, moving over R$20M (about $3.9M) in suspicious funds. Target: Brazilian consumers. BR. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Brasilia police Operacao VoiceOver busts gang using Marcos Mion deepfakes for voucher scam
item.description: The Policia Civil do Distrito Federal arrested three people aged 20 to 23 who used deepfake video and voice of TV host Marcos Mion in sponsored ads for fake Outback discount vouchers sold on cloned sites. Target: Brazilian consumers. BR. Verification: confirmed.
